sections.h2: Which Bainbridge desks handle Decatur County property tax?
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices in Bainbridge split the job. One office prepares the digest, mails the bills and takes payment. The other, the assessors, puts a value on every real and personal parcel. Both operate inside the courthouse on West Water Street.

Collection happens on the ground floor of the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Monday to Friday between 8 and 5. Call (229) 248-3021 about property tax, (229) 248-3019 for motor vehicles or (229) 248-3009 for the tag office. Letters go to P.O. Box 246, Bainbridge, and decaturcountytax.com is the office's website. Valuation questions go to (229) 248-3008 or to P.O. Box 1106 in the same city.

Roughly 20,000 property tax bills and 3,300 mobile home bills go out each year, according to the collector's site. What comes in is sent on to the state, county, schools, library and cities every other week.

sections.h2: How does the geography of Decatur County affect a sale?
sections.html:
Decatur County is the largest of the four Georgia counties in the Census comparison, with 623 square miles, of which about 597 are land. It reaches the Florida line on its southern edge, and Bainbridge holds the courthouse. The county makes up the Bainbridge micropolitan area, one piece of the Tallahassee and Bainbridge combined statistical area.

Most of the county drains to the lower Flint River around Bainbridge. The southwestern corner near Attapulgus drains toward the Ochlockonee, and a sliver in the far southwest reaches the Apalachicola. U.S. 27, U.S. 84 and State Routes 97, 241, 253, 262, 285, 302, 309, 310 and 311 carry traffic. Miller, Mitchell, Baker, Grady and Seminole counties border it, and Gadsden County, Florida, lies to the south.

Attapulgus, Bainbridge and Climax are cities, Brinson is a town, and Faceville is a census-designated place. Amsterdam, Ausmac and Cyrene are unincorporated communities. The county dates to December 8, 1823, when it was split from Early County, and it later gave up land to Thomas, Grady and Seminole counties. Because several cities lie inside the county, check whether your parcel also owes a city bill.

sections.h2: What do the newest Census figures say about Decatur County housing?
sections.html:
Headcount here has been flat lately. Census figures were 27,842 in 2010 and 29,367 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 29,432 compares with a revised 2020 base of 29,479.

  • Housing units: 13,601, with 10,621 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.1 percent.
  • Value of the typical owned home, 2020 to 2024: $158,800.
  • Typical rent: $838 monthly.
  • Income for the midpoint household: $53,317, with 21.7 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Housing permits in 2025: 135.
  • Mean commute: 21.4 minutes.

The county has 626 employer establishments and 7,687 employees as of 2023, up 2.8 percent from the year before. Its transportation and warehousing receipts of about $60.6 million in 2022 were the highest of the four counties compared. Retail sales were about $451 million, or $15,551 per resident, well below the figure for Crisp or Dawson County.

sections.h2: What are the key tax dates in Decatur County?
sections.html:
Decatur County sets December 20 as the yearly deadline for property tax and April 1 for mobile homes. Both dates are on the county's commissioner pages.

Decatur County tax dates and contacts (source: Decatur County tax commissioner and tax assessor pages)
ItemDetail
Real and personal property billsDue December 20
Mobile home billsDue April 1
Returns, conservation and agricultural applicationsJanuary 1 through April 1
Homestead applicationDuring the year, up to April 1 of the following year per the assessors' notice
Appeal of an assessment45 days from the mailing date printed on the notice
Board of Assessors meetingSecond Tuesday of each month, 8:30 a.m., Grand Jury Room

The state revenue department says a county can choose December 1 or November 15 instead, or bill in installments, and that interest holds off for 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Ask the commissioner what interest and penalties apply to a late bill.

sections.h2: How are appeals and exemption forms submitted in Decatur County?
sections.html:
Look at the top right corner of the assessment notice. The county prints the final appeal day there, 45 days after mailing, and it moves from year to year, so rely on your own paper.

The assessors' office also receives returns for real and personal property and applications for homestead, conservation use, preferential agricultural assessment, forest land conservation use assessment and Freeport. Blank forms sit on the Department of Revenue's forms page, and completed ones can go in by email, ordinary mail or the drop box outside the courthouse.

  • Returns and special-use applications: January 1 through April 1.
  • Homestead under Code Section 48-5-44: the application may be filed once the house is your primary residence, through April 1 of the next year.
  • Property records and parcel data: the county's qPublic site at qpublic.net/ga/decatur.
  • Board sessions: second Tuesday monthly, 8:30 in the morning, Grand Jury Room.

sections.h2: Will an appraiser visit my Decatur County property?
sections.html:
Possibly. A public notice from the assessors cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, which allows representatives with proper identification to enter property during normal business hours. Reasons include permits that were issued, a return of value, a revaluation of part or all of the county, parcel sales and appeal reviews.

The office says it uses building permits and other sources to update its records, and that appraisers visit where improvements were made or information looks wrong. If you added a room, finished a garage or tore something down, the permit trail may already have reached the assessors, so a seller should check what the record says before a buyer's agent does.

The assessors also assemble the tax digest, which is the compilation of property values, motor vehicle values, timber values and exemption amounts that goes to the State Revenue Commissioner. A change in your parcel's record flows into that report.

sections.h2: What if a Decatur County seller owes back tax or a mobile home bill?
sections.html:
Only the commissioner can quote a payoff. Phone (229) 248-3021, give the parcel number and your expected closing date, and ask for the number in writing.

  • A mobile home has its own April 1 bill, so check that account separately from any land.
  • Cities in the county levy their own tax, and the state says the city clerk bills it unless the city and county agreed to a single bill. Ask the commissioner whether yours is combined.
  • Refunds for tax wrongly collected must be requested within three years of the payment.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask the assessors which documents they need to update the owner before the bill goes out.

Bills are charged to the owner on January 1 under Georgia's rules, so the sale contract should state who covers the portion of the year after closing. Have the settlement agent send the payoff directly to the commissioner and keep the receipt.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Decatur County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Bainbridge, GA 39817, first floor. The counter runs weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax number is (229) 248-3021.

faqs.q: What is the Decatur County payment deadline?
faqs.a: December 20, the commissioner's page says, with mobile homes due April 1. Confirm against your own bill, since a county may adopt another date.

faqs.q: How many days does a Decatur County owner have to appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days counted from the mailing date of the notice. The last filing day is printed in the notice's top right corner.

faqs.q: Does Decatur County have a drop box for tax forms?
faqs.a: Yes. The assessors list a drop box outside the courthouse, along with email and regular mail, as ways to submit forms and applications.

faqs.q: How large is Decatur County compared with its neighbors in Georgia?
faqs.a: Decatur County covers 623 square miles, with about 597 of them land. That is the largest of the four Georgia counties compared in the Census table, where Crawford, Crisp and Dawson cover roughly 325, 273 and 211 square miles of land.
